title: History Has No Chill
blurb: Presidents, scientists, emperors and composers, with true stories too weird to make up.

cards.say: John Adams [was the first president to live in the White House], [lived in the White House for all four years of his presidency], [left town before the man who beat him was sworn in], and [died on the very same day as Thomas Jefferson].
cards.real: Adams moved into the unfinished White House on November 1, 1800, with only about four months left in his term.
src: https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/november-1/john-adams-moves-into-white-house (moved in November 1, 1800; Jefferson sworn in March 4, 1801)
https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/november-1/john-adams-moves-into-white-house (as Jefferson was sworn in, Adams was already on his way back to Massachusetts)

cards.say: James Madison [stood just 5 feet 4 inches tall], [once suggested hiring Portugal's navy to fight pirates], [has his face on the 5,000 dollar bill], and [lost a 1789 race for Congress to James Monroe].
cards.real: Madison beat James Monroe for a seat in the first House of Representatives in 1789. Monroe later followed him as president.
src: https://www.mentalfloss.com/history/presidents/16-fun-facts-james-madisons-birthday (he defeated Monroe for a House seat in 1789)

cards.say: Ulysses S. Grant [graduated first in his class at West Point], [was born with the first name Hiram], [was arrested for speeding in his horse carriage while president], and [signed the law that made Yellowstone the first national park].
cards.real: Grant finished 21st out of 39 cadets in West Point's class of 1843, strong in math and science but weak in military subjects.

cards.say: Franklin D. Roosevelt [moved Thanksgiving up a week in 1939 to help stores], [was the first president to appear on television], [was the first president ever heard on the radio], and [had a dog who got his own statue at the FDR Memorial].
cards.real: Presidents were on the radio before FDR: Calvin Coolidge's December 1923 speech to Congress went out over the air. FDR made it famous with fireside chats.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge (December 6, 1923 address broadcast over the radio, ten years before FDR took office)
https://www.nps.gov/articles/fala.htm (Fala is the only presidential pet so honored)

cards.say: Calvin Coolidge [was born on the Fourth of July], [adopted a raccoon that was sent to be his Thanksgiving dinner], [was sworn in as president by his own father, by lamplight], and [served as governor of Vermont before he became president].
cards.real: Coolidge was born in Vermont but made his career in Massachusetts, where he was governor from 1919 to 1921.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge (his father, a notary public, gave the oath by kerosene lamp on August 3, 1923)

cards.say: Isaac Newton [was born on the very day that Galileo died], [hunted down counterfeiters while working at England's Royal Mint], [was knighted by Queen Anne in 1705], and [served two short terms in Parliament].
cards.real: Galileo died on January 8, 1642. Newton was born almost a year later, on Christmas Day 1642 by England's old calendar.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (Warden then Master of the Royal Mint; prosecuted 28 coiners)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (MP for Cambridge University 1689 to 1690 and 1701 to 1702)

cards.say: Albert Einstein [turned down an offer to be president of Israel], [hated socks so much that he refused to wear them], [won his Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity], and [was such a bad sailor that his neighbors had to rescue him].
cards.real: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics was for explaining the photoelectric effect, work very different from relativity.
src: https://www.livescience.com/physics-mathematics/32-fun-and-random-facts-about-albert-einstein (neighbors often had to rescue him when his boat capsized)

cards.say: Napoleon [wrote a romance novella years before he became emperor], [had his soldiers shoot the nose off Egypt's Great Sphinx], [stood about 5 foot 6, taller than the average Frenchman then], and [died before anyone took a photo that still survives today].
cards.real: Drawings from 1737 already show the Sphinx without its nose, decades before Napoleon was born. His army reached Egypt in 1798.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/View_from_the_Window_at_Le_Gras (oldest surviving camera photo, 1826 or 1827; Napoleon died 1821, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon)

cards.say: The French Revolution [freed more than 100 prisoners when crowds stormed the Bastille], [briefly used official clocks with 10 hours in a day], [gave the world the metric system], and [began the same year George Washington became president].
cards.real: When crowds stormed the Bastille on July 14, 1789, the old fortress prison held just seven prisoners.

cards.say: Ludwig van Beethoven [has no known birthday, only the date he was baptized], [scratched Napoleon's name off a symphony he had named after him], [had to be turned around to see the crowd cheering his Ninth Symphony], and [moved to Vienna in 1792 to take lessons from Mozart].
cards.real: Mozart had died in December 1791. When Beethoven moved to Vienna in 1792, he studied with Joseph Haydn instead.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (Eroica, first titled Bonaparte; name scratched off in 1804)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (7 May 1824 premiere; Caroline Unger turned him around to see the applause)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (moved to Vienna November 1792 after the recent death of Mozart; studied with Haydn)

cards.say: Peter the Great [stood about 6 feet 8 inches tall], [worked four months in a Dutch shipyard under a fake name], [moved Russia's New Year's Day from January 1 to September 1], and [shaved the beards off his own party guests with a razor].
cards.real: It was the other way around: in 1699, Peter moved Russia's New Year from September 1 to January 1.
src: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/why-tsar-peter-great-established-beard-tax-180964693/ (traveled as Sergeant Pyotr Mikhaylov; four months at a Dutch East India Company shipyard)
https://mdwiki.org/wiki/Peter_the_Great (in 1699 moved the New Year from 1 September to 1 January)

cards.say: Ada Lovelace [never met her father, the famous poet Lord Byron], [saw her program run on Charles Babbage's finished Analytical Engine], [wrote what historians call the first computer program, in 1843], and [predicted that computing machines could one day make music].
cards.real: Babbage's Analytical Engine was never finished. Only a small piece of it was ever built, so her program never ran in her lifetime.
src: https://www.britannica.com/story/ada-lovelace-the-first-computer-programmer (only a small piece of the engine was ever built)
https://www.britannica.com/story/ada-lovelace-the-first-computer-programmer (engine could work on things besides number, such as musical notes)
